articles.title: Propofol increases baseline-referenced spectral-state displacement: an exploratory analysis
articles.source_path: Apollo_propofol_ndt_v.1.0/Propofol increases baseline-referenced spectral-state displacement.typ
articles.abstract: An exploratory reanalysis of 20 Cambridge propofol EEG participants measures radial displacement from pre-drug baseline in a fixed eight-feature chart. Displacement rose during sedation and remained above baseline in recovery; the analysis describes state relocation, not a matched-state change in future dynamics.
takeaways: Displacement rose in 18/20 participants at first sedation and 20/20 at later sedation.
Median changes were +1.70 and +5.92; recovery remained elevated at +1.34.
The measure does not establish a change in conditional future law.

articles.title: Early Changes in Infant EEG State-Space Geometry: An Exploratory Longitudinal Reanalysis
articles.source_path: APPLESEED_infants/Early Changes in Infant EEG State-Space Geometry.typ
articles.abstract: This study assesses reproducibility and early longitudinal change in 48 EEG recordings from 13 infants using a shared cohort anchor and child-session summaries. Test-retest estimates were heterogeneous; no primary 3D dynamical endpoint survived correction at eight or twelve months, while an exploratory twelve-month mobility contrast declined.
takeaways: The shared anchor used 8,179 epochs; inference used one summary per child-session.
No primary 3D dynamical endpoint survived BH-FDR at either age.
Mobility declined in all 11 children in the balanced 12-month panel, a chart-level result rather than a maturational mechanism.

articles.title: Registered descriptive reanalysis of BOAS sleep-stage geometry
articles.source_path: BOAS_sleep_dataset_ndt._v.1.0/manuscript.typ
articles.abstract: This exploratory registered reanalysis audits support for local-Jacobian, finite-time-response, and newer dynamical-family outputs in a stage-sampled BOAS run. It reports descriptive stage contrasts while retaining gaps and unavailable products; the manuscript sets a method-limited interpretation ceiling.
takeaways: The run has 128 recording IDs from 100 people and 16,629 selected 30-second windows, with 1,469 sampling gaps.
Finite-time response was available at all registered horizons in 3D and for 126/128 recordings in 9D.
The diffusion parent was not testable with irregular increment timing; this is not an independent confirmation or a C1-C3 test.

articles.title: Resting-State Neural Geometry in Alzheimer Disease and Frontotemporal Dementia
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/alzheimer/AD_FTD_article.typ
articles.abstract: A fixed NeuralManifoldDynamics workflow compares healthy, Alzheimer disease, and frontotemporal dementia groups in resting EEG. Selected block-Jacobian summaries showed clearer group differences than coarse global summaries, while the strongest severity associations were concentrated in FTD.
takeaways: Selected d-to-d block magnitude differed for both dementia groups versus healthy controls; AD versus FTD was weak.
FTD showed MMSE associations with 9D spectral radius and e-to-e block magnitude.
Conclusions are limited to this dataset and export surface.

articles.title: Evoked Neural Geometry Under Photic Stress in Alzheimer Disease and Frontotemporal Dementia
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/alzheimer_ftd_photonic/Evoked Neural Geometry Under Photic Stress in Alzheimer Disease and Frontotemporal Dementia.typ
articles.abstract: This analysis compares ds006036 photic EEG with matched ds004504 resting references. Corrected group differences were narrow: AD-versus-healthy separation appeared on global 9D MNJ at selected stimulation frequencies, while the matching resting contrast was near null and FTD group contrasts did not survive correction.
takeaways: The strongest corrected AD-versus-healthy row was 9D mdr_median at 20 Hz, with rows also at 10 and 15 Hz.
The same resting-state contrast was near null.
Severity associations were broader and concentrated in high-frequency global 9D measures.

articles.title: Evoked Structural Brittleness Under Photic Stimulation in Alzheimer Disease and Frontotemporal Dementia
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/alzheimer_ftd_photonic_esb/Evoked Structural Brittleness Under Photic Stimulation in Alzheimer Disease and Frontotemporal Dementia.typ
articles.abstract: This follow-up defines an exploratory ESB-2 response-deviation score from photic EEG and matched resting baselines. AD and FTD differed from healthy responses most clearly at 15 Hz; the manuscript bounds this internally stabilized result to the current cohort.
takeaways: ESB-2 combined posterior effective dimensionality and global rotational power after baseline subtraction.
AD-versus-healthy and FTD-versus-healthy contrasts at 15 Hz survived correction and remained smaller but present after cross-fitting.
The deviation was mainly capacity-led; the secondary PRL test was negative.
The score is not an externally validated biomarker or resonance-loss theorem.

articles.title: Recovery-Linked Neural Geometry After Cardiac-Arrest Coma
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/comatose_ndt/Recovery-Linked Neural Geometry After Cardiac-Arrest Coma.typ
articles.abstract: A two-cohort I-CARE analysis asks whether short-horizon EEG geometry distinguishes later CPC 1 from CPC 5 outcomes in the first twelve hours after EEG anchor. Five prespecified reachability measures were significant in pooled analysis; the authors do not claim a unique decisive hour or bedside readiness.
takeaways: The pooled extreme-outcome contrast included 281 patients from non-overlapping cohorts.
All five prespecified reachability metrics survived pooled BH-FDR.
Effective dimensionality differed in the first hour, but a circular-shift null did not support a precise peak-hour claim.
AUROC improved against a restricted clinical-plus-qEEG baseline, not full multimodal prognostication.

articles.title: Outcome-Linked 9D Jacobian Geometry After Cardiac-Arrest Coma
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/comatose_ndt/comatose_old_9d/comatose_ndt_jacobian_9d/Outcome-Linked 9D Jacobian Geometry After Cardiac-Arrest Coma.typ
articles.abstract: This companion I-CARE analysis tests whether repaired 9D local-linear summaries add outcome-linked information beyond reachability. Spectral radius was the clearest replicated Jacobian measure; incremental prediction was modest and unavailable clinical annotations constrain interpretation.
takeaways: Spectral-radius differences replicated directionally in both cohorts.
Anisotropy also replicated directionally but with cohort asymmetry; Frobenius norm was a stable comparator.
Adding revised 9D measures gave a small AUROC increment over clinical, qEEG, and reachability features.
The manuscript frames 9D as complementary, not a replacement for clinical assessment.

articles.title: Block-Jacobian Coupling in Early Cardiac-Arrest Coma
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/comatose_block_jacobian/comatose_block_jacobian.typ
articles.abstract: This interim follow-up tests whether blocks of a repaired 9x9 Jacobian differ by later outcome during the first twelve hours after EEG anchor. In the part1 discovery export, better-outcome patients showed lower diagonal and selected cross-family magnitudes; part2 verification and pooled synthesis were pending.
takeaways: The discovery export retained 141 extreme-outcome patients despite 88 upstream failed groupings.
Lower diagonal block Frobenius magnitude was the clearest provisional result; ee, dd, and ed summaries were also lower.
Directional asymmetry remained exploratory.
The source describes an interim discovery draft, not a replication-complete result.

articles.title: Outcome-Linked Geometric Trajectory After Cardiac-Arrest Coma
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/comatose_geometric_trajectory/Outcome-Linked Geometric Trajectory After Cardiac-Arrest Coma.typ
articles.abstract: This exploratory study measures irreversibility, repertoire entropy rate, and noetic action in 3D and 9D coma EEG trajectories. Pooled signals did not survive BH-FDR, and time-shuffle checks indicated that noetic action primarily reflected trajectory roughness rather than temporal order.
takeaways: The workflow covered separate part1 and part2 cohorts plus pooled robustness checks.
No article-facing trajectory metric survived BH-FDR; 9D noetic action was the clearest pooled signal.
Noetic-action effects strengthened under time shuffle, which argues against reading them as temporal grammar.
3D irreversibility attenuated and correlated with channel-coverage QC.

articles.title: Recovery-Linked Neural Geometry 12-24 h Pilot After Cardiac-Arrest Coma
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/comatose_ndt_12_24/Recovery-Linked Neural Geometry 12-24 h Pilot After Cardiac-Arrest Coma.typ
articles.abstract: This pilot extends the established coma contract into the 12-24-hour window. Three of five reachability measures survived within-family correction with mixed directions, while effective dimensionality and Jacobian anchors were modest; strict between-run variability was not testable in the sparse late-window subset.
takeaways: Only 143 runs from 97 subjects belonged to the true 12-24-hour slice.
Persistence, operator-norm, and capture-gate measures survived correction with mixed directions; effective dimensionality did not.
The strict three-run variability threshold was not testable.
The paper is a late-window pilot, not evidence of a uniform time course.

articles.title: Regional reachability geometry after cardiac-arrest coma (draft)
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/comatose_ndt_regional/comatose_ndt_regional_draft.typ
articles.abstract: This results-ready draft proposes a regional follow-up to the I-CARE analysis, retaining its outcome contract, time window, and metric families while comparing predefined scalp channel groups. Regional export finalization was pending, so the manuscript reports no completed regional effects.
takeaways: Planned channel groups are frontal, central, parietal-occipital, temporal, midline, and left/right hemisphere.
Planned summaries cover effective dimensionality, persistence, and capture/operator norm.
The question is where recovery-linked divergence appears during the first twelve hours.
Results await the regional export handoff.

articles.title: Resting-State Neural Geometry Across Depressive Symptom Burden
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/depression/Resting-State Neural Geometry Across Depressive Symptom Burden.typ
articles.abstract: This fixed-workflow analysis of ds003478 resting EEG uses Beck Depression Inventory scores to compare selected global, stratified, Jacobian, and reachability measures. Symptom separation was clearer in reachability, 9D MNJ, and distribution summaries than in coarse 3D coordinates, and was more consistent with a low-to-elevated regime contrast than a monotonic gradient.
takeaways: Low-versus-high BDI differences concentrated in reachability, 9D rotational power, and an entropy-memory distribution summary.
Continuous BDI analyses retained the same broad ordering, with reachability and 9D summaries stronger than 3D.
The 0-13 versus 14-19 contrast was stronger than the 14-19 versus 20-63 contrast.
This is a bounded analysis in one cohort, not a diagnostic biomarker study.

articles.title: Depressive Symptom Geometry Across Rest and Probabilistic Selection
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/depression_probalistic_selection/Depressive Symptom Geometry Across Rest and Probabilistic Selection.typ
articles.abstract: This paired analysis combines probabilistic-selection EEG and resting EEG for participants with BDI data. Symptoms were associated with task-state reachability and block-resolved 9D dynamics, while paired task-minus-rest summaries and event-locked contrasts did not support a strong symptom-dependent reconfiguration claim.
takeaways: The paired metadata overlap was 122 participants, with 121 usable BDI scores.
Task-state reachability and e-to-d block-Jacobian structure had the clearest corrected symptom associations.
The selected paired task-minus-rest surface was broadly null.
Event-locked effects did not survive FDR correction.

articles.title: Event-First Reinforcement-Learning Geometry Across Depressive Symptom Burden
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/depression_probalistic_selection_event/Event-First Reinforcement-Learning Geometry Across Depressive Symptom Burden.typ
articles.abstract: This event-first reanalysis reconstructs trial-local trajectory summaries from existing probabilistic-selection event windows. Correct-versus-incorrect feedback showed corrected differences in path length, kinetic cost, and hysteresis; certainty and symptom-modulation contrasts did not survive correction.
takeaways: The primary feedback contrast was evaluated across 122 participants.
Path length, noetic-action kinetic cost, and hysteresis were the leading corrected event-native effects.
The high- versus low-certainty contrast was not significant after FDR.
Train-versus-test effects were lower priority, and BDI modulation remained uncorrected.

articles.title: First-Episode Psychosis Geometry Across Two Resting-State EEG Cohorts
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/psychosis_first_time_episode/First-Episode Psychosis Geometry Across Two Resting-State EEG Cohorts.typ
articles.abstract: This shared-reference analysis compares healthy, unmedicated FEP, and medicated FEP groups in two resting EEG cohorts. The signal-bearing family differed by cohort: m-family shifts in medicated cases led one cohort, while reduced drift in the small unmedicated group led the other; the paper presents an analysis surface rather than a universal biomarker.
takeaways: In ds003944, corrected effects were led by m-family displacement in medicated cases versus healthy controls.
In ds003947, reduced trajectory drift in unmedicated cases was the strongest corrected result, with eight unmedicated participants.
Pooled sensitivity weakened the second cohort’s dynamic effect, supporting medication-stratified reporting.
Some subgroup separation also appeared in conventional spectral and complexity summaries.

articles.title: Medication-Stratified Trajectory Geometry in First-Episode Psychosis
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/psychosis_first_time_geometric_trajectory/psychosis_first_time_geometric_trajectory.typ
articles.abstract: This companion analysis examines movement through subject-anchored 3D and 9D EEG charts in two FEP cohorts. Trajectory action and entropy measures partly dissociated from the static-coordinate pattern, but the evidence was limited and the second cohort underpowered.
takeaways: In ds003944, unmedicated cases had the largest trajectory-action effects, narrowly missing the stated BH-FDR threshold.
No contrast reached correction in ds003947.
The trajectory and static analyses suggested a possible medication-related dissociation across layers.
The manuscript describes the results as exploratory and power-limited.

articles.title: Functional-Family Block Coupling in First-Episode Psychosis
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/psychosis_first_time_block_jacobian/functional_family_coupling_psychosis.typ
articles.abstract: This analysis decomposes local linear dynamics in two FEP EEG cohorts into 9x9 block-Jacobian summaries for metastability, diffusivity, and entropy families. Medication-stratified coupling patterns differed by cohort and were presented as complementary to static coordinates and trajectories.
takeaways: In ds003944, entropic self-coupling followed a healthy-to-unmedicated-to-medicated gradient, with medicated values above healthy controls.
In ds003947, the clearest replication signal was reduced diffusivity self-coupling in unmedicated cases.
Metastability-to-entropy and directed diffusivity-entropy coupling also differed in medicated ds003944 cases.
The authors describe reorganization rather than simple medication normalization.

articles.title: Auditory Oddball Occupies a Compressed Event-Locked Trajectory Regime in a Behavior-Enriched EEG Cohort
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/parkinson_auditory_recall/Auditory Oddball Occupies a Compressed Event-Locked Trajectory Regime in a Behavior-Enriched EEG Cohort.typ
articles.abstract: This event-first ds004574 analysis compares subtype-aware auditory oddball and standard windows in subject-anchored trajectories, treating Parkinson-control structure as secondary. Auditory windows showed a compressed trajectory regime, strongest around arrow cues; no event-locked Parkinson-control contrast survived correction.
takeaways: Auditory windows had lower entropy rate, path length, and peak displacement and higher transition sparsity than standard windows.
The strongest corrected row was the 9D arrow-cue entropy-rate contrast.
Auditory-versus-visual and event-locked Parkinson-versus-control contrasts did not survive BH-FDR.
Smaller Parkinson differences remained in standard global summaries.

articles.title: Task Canalization Hides Disease-Facing Cost and Coupling Trends in Parkinson EEG
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/parkinson_oddball_geometric_trajectory/Task Canalization Hides Disease-Facing Cost and Coupling Trends in Parkinson EEG.typ
articles.abstract: This disease-first ds004574 reanalysis expands event-centered summaries to include family temporal coupling. No event-locked Parkinson-control contrast survived correction; retained disease differences were global, while subtype effects remained much larger than disease-facing wrapper effects.
takeaways: Event-wrapper trends involved coupling and recovery but none survived BH-FDR.
Lower global 3D m and higher reachability q-ratio were retained Parkinson-control differences.
Auditory-versus-standard subtype effects remained much larger than disease-facing wrapper effects.
The manuscript does not support an event-locked Parkinson biomarker.

articles.title: Task Context Determines How Much Parkinson Disease-State Geometry Is Recoverable
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/parkinson_cognitive_workload_ON_OFF/Task Context Determines How Much Parkinson Disease-State Geometry Is Recoverable.typ
articles.abstract: This comparison applies a fixed mixed-contract analysis to Simon-conflict and reinforcement-learning EEG datasets with repeated Parkinson ON/OFF recordings. Disease-state geometry was broad in Simon conflict and thinner, with more overlap with conventional alpha summaries, in reinforcement learning; medication and event-level effects were weak.
takeaways: Simon conflict retained broad corrected disease-state geometry plus a secondary Jacobian/reachability branch.
Reinforcement learning retained fewer effects, led partly by relative alpha and a smaller Jacobian branch.
Paired medication contrasts were weak in both datasets.
No event-locked wrapper row survived q < 0.1.

articles.title: Shared-Reference Disease-State Geometry Exceeds Paired Pharmacology Effects in Parkinson ON OFF Auditory Oddball EEG
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/parkinson_on_off_trajectory/Shared-Reference Disease-State Geometry Exceeds Paired Pharmacology Effects in Parkinson ON OFF Auditory Oddball EEG.typ
articles.abstract: This mixed-contract ds003490 reanalysis separates between-person Parkinson-control comparisons from within-person medication ON-OFF comparisons. Disease-state geometry remained broad across standard and event-locked layers, while paired medication effects were narrow and hypothesis-generating.
takeaways: The analysis included 75 runs: 25 Parkinson ON/OFF pairs and 25 controls.
Forty-seven rows survived q < 0.05, including 35 standard and 12 event-locked rows; no trajectory ESB row survived.
The strongest findings were shared-reference disease-state and eyes-closed trajectory contrasts.
Only one row survived correction in the paired medication contrast.

articles.title: Walking-State Geometry Separates Parkinson Disease from Controls More Clearly Than Paired Rest-to-Walk Reconfiguration
articles.source_path: CLINICAL/parkinson_walking/Walking-State Geometry Separates Parkinson Disease from Controls More Clearly Than Paired Rest-to-Walk Reconfiguration.typ
articles.abstract: This ds007526 analysis treats Parkinson-versus-control walking as a cohort-anchored comparison and rest-to-walk changes as subject-anchored. Four corrected disease-state rows appeared in the global diffusivity family; a dispersion extension strengthened the paired Parkinson branch, and the export lacked conventional EEG comparators.
takeaways: The cohort-walk signal was concentrated in four global d-family rows.
Adding IQR and MAD summaries strengthened paired Parkinson rest-to-walk contrasts.
The strongest clinical associations were in rest-side dispersion measures.
No classical-comparator claim was possible because conventional EEG was absent from the bundle.

articles.title: Neural flow geometry differentiates gambling and cognitive control despite matched sympathetic arousal
articles.source_path: Neural flow geometry differentiates gambling and cognitive control/Neural flow geometry differentiates gambling and cognitive control despite matched sympathetic arousal.typ
articles.abstract: This multimodal ds004511 analysis compares gambling, cognitive-control, and rest conditions using MNPS coordinates and local Jacobian metrics. Global coordinates did not separate the active tasks, but local flow geometry did; the contrast remained after tested peripheral-arousal and signal-confound checks.
takeaways: Across 57,526 epochs, global MNPS coordinates did not separate the tasks.
Gambling-versus-control differences were large in Jacobian Frobenius norm and spectral radius.
The contrast was not explained by the tested EDA, corrugator EMG, spectral-power, or stimulus/response measures.
The secondary respiratory-anchoring association did not survive correction.

articles.title: Task Contrasts Dissociate Across Neural-Dynamics Estimators
articles.source_path: ds04511_ndt_v.1.0/Task Contrasts Dissociate Across Neural-Dynamics Estimators.typ
articles.abstract: This ds004511 analysis compares rest, cognitive control, and gambling across estimator families on a subject-anchored chart. Local L1 drift, local chart-Jacobian, independently identified one-step, and recording-level reachability summaries behaved differently; duration and support limits constrain interpretation.
takeaways: Local drift magnitude showed the clearest task hierarchy and persisted in a 400-second prefix sensitivity.
The local chart-Jacobian spectral abscissa increased for gambling versus rest, while the one-step analogue did not.
Chart and local-drift task contrasts were inversely associated on common support and agreed in sign for only 12/32 pairs.
Reachability was unavailable for three certificates and exported as recording-level scalars.

articles.title: EEG-MEG Concordance of Neural-Manifold Feature Surfaces in Healthy Adults
articles.source_path: eeg_meg_task/manuscript.typ
articles.abstract: This study compares matched EEG and MEG feature surfaces in 18 people from the simultaneous FacePerception cohort. Temporal agreement varied by feature family and topology, while subject-level means retained modality offsets; export-quality findings limited the regional geometry interpretation.
takeaways: The analysis included 108 participant-run exports.
Feature and topology choices changed temporal concordance; average values retained modality offsets.
All six EEG regional MNPS trajectories were identical within each run and were not treated as independent regional measures.
The global EEG chart was a MEG-primary shadow mapping, so symmetric regional inference awaits a corrected export.

articles.title: Hypoglycemia Reshapes Stratified Neural Dynamics in a Validity-Bounded Paired Analysis
articles.source_path: hypoglycemia_metabolic_anchoring/manuscript.typ
articles.abstract: A paired reanalysis of five-minute EEG excerpts from 34 people with type 1 diabetes compares hypoglycemia with euglycemia using fixed 3D and stratified 9D charts. Several chart components changed, while reachability was validity-limited and not treated as confirmatory.
takeaways: Three-dimensional mobility decreased in the paired hypoglycemia contrast.
Several 9D coordinates changed, and raw EEG checks showed theta/delta and entropy shifts.
Label-swap and adjusted-geometry sensitivities preserved directions in the prespecified 9D panel.
The results do not establish a dose-response, recovery trajectory, metabolic gate, or reachability effect.

articles.title: Cardiorespiratory anchor indices and neural manifold geometry during visual-illusion perception
articles.source_path: illusionGame_EAP/manuscript.typ
articles.abstract: This audit asks whether OpenNeuro ds004587 can test cardiorespiratory anchoring during visual-illusion perception. The accessible export lacked resting EEG, trial labels, time-reference provenance, and block-native windows; after a scale-defect fix, no available anchor association survived correction.
takeaways: The export contained 57 recordings from 47 participants but lacked key rest and event-alignment inputs.
A corrected export fixed a degenerate robust-z scale affecting one anchor and its composite index.
No direct or HRV-adjusted anchor association with MNPS/MNJ summaries survived BH-FDR.
The results neither validate nor refute the causal Embodied Anchoring Principle.

articles.title: Cohort-Anchored Infant EEG State-Space Geometry Tracks Age in Early Infancy
articles.source_path: infant_eeg/Cohort-Anchored Infant EEG State-Space Geometry Tracks Age in Early Infancy.typ
articles.abstract: This reanalysis studies age-associated change in 70 artifact-masked EEG recordings from 22 infants using a frozen cohort chart. Within-child coordinate associations appeared, but conservative permutation checks supported only part of that surface; local-dynamics families lacked corrected age effects while conventional qEEG comparators were stronger.
takeaways: Artifact masking retained 5,265 of 6,929 candidate epochs.
The spline model found within-child coordinate associations, but only 6/12 endpoints survived stricter permutation correction.
Neither within-child nor pooled local-dynamics tests showed FDR-supported age effects.
Classical qEEG comparators showed more robust age associations.

articles.title: Noetic Diffusion Theory: A Rhythmic, Geometric Framework for Neural State Reconstruction and Conscious Correlates
articles.source_path: NDT/NoeticDiffusionTheory.typ
articles.abstract: This manuscript presents NDT as a testable framework in which rhythmically scheduled stochastic denoising unfolds on a learned geometric manifold. It defines a proposed Meta-Noetic Diffusion Model, Rhythmic Variance Control, and MNPS, while distinguishing empirical targets from a complete theory of subjective experience.
takeaways: The proposed model uses a guided stochastic differential equation with a rhythmic variance schedule.
MNPS is introduced as an operational chart with mobility, diffusivity, and entropy-related axes.
Proposed tests include event-linked entropy change, sleep-stage topology, and disorder-related geometry.
NDHI is described as exploratory, not a clinical biomarker or consciousness score.

articles.title: Noetic Diffusion Theory: A Meso-to-Macro Geometry of Neural State Reconstruction
articles.source_path: NDT_2/ndt_2.typ
articles.abstract: This theoretical manuscript develops a meso-to-macro account in which rhythmic neural activity may gate stochastic flow on a measured chart. It distinguishes proposed mechanisms from evidence, discusses cross-scale measurements and a truth-known simulator, and presents embodied anchoring and metabolic adequacy as hypotheses.
takeaways: The text links mesoscopic thalamocortical and population signals to macroscopic EEG/MEG/fMRI charts.
Companion Neuropixels-EEG results are described as bounded association evidence, not Jacobian or reachability validation.
A truth-known simulator separates association, mechanism discrimination, latent-order preservation, and operator recovery.
The biological mappings remain hypotheses to test against simpler alternatives.

articles.title: Noetic Diffusion Theory: Neural State, Dynamical Accessibility, and the Geometry of Possible Futures
articles.source_path: NoeticDiffusionTheory_v2_cognitive_neurodynamics/Noetic Diffusion Theory - Neural State, Dynamical Accessibility, and the Geometry of Possible Futures.typ
articles.abstract: This revised theory manuscript organizes neural dynamics around present state and conditional future law. It separates established tools from proposed tests, treats charts as operational interfaces to latent dynamics, and uses synthetic examples to distinguish accessibility questions without claiming neural validation.
takeaways: The framework asks whether future-law summaries add held-out value beyond present chart location and ordinary signal summaries.
It distinguishes short-horizon spread, first-hit events, committors, representation validity, and operator recovery.
Synthetic examples validate distinctions on known systems, not biological mechanisms.
NDT is not presented as a consciousness scalar or an explanation of subjective experience.

articles.title: NeuralManifoldDynamics: A Versioned Measurement Contract for Low-Dimensional Neural-Manifold Trajectories
articles.source_path: NeuralManifoldDynamics/NeuralManifoldDynamics A Versioned Measurement Contract for Low-Dimensional Neural-Manifold Trajectories.typ
articles.abstract: This methods manuscript describes NeuralManifoldDynamics 2.4 as an auditable ingest contract for EEG, MEG, fMRI, and selected feature-table sources. It fixes a canonical 3D chart, supports optional 9D and Jacobian exports, and emphasizes support, validity, anchoring, provenance, and the distinction between exported measures and theoretical constructs.
takeaways: The contract preserves canonical 3D [m,d,e] ordering and an optional stratified 9D chart.
Versioned outputs expose coverage, non-finite support, validity, provenance, and coordinate anchoring.
Embodied and MEG-derived surfaces are additive layers and do not redefine the canonical chart.
The contribution is a reusable measurement contract, not superior latent-state discovery.

articles.title: Neural State Geometry and Dynamical Measurement Families Across Sleep
articles.source_path: ndt_v3_sleep/Neural State Geometry and Dynamical Measurement Families Across Sleep.typ
articles.abstract: This full-cohort descriptive study analyzes PSG from 100 people across 128 nights and compares selected local-Jacobian and diffusion measurement families between N2 and Wake. Several recording-relative measures shared directional contrasts, while dimensionality and concentration were more heterogeneous; temporal support and coordinate references limit interpretation.
takeaways: Continuous 30-second processing produced 120,091 epochs aligned to scored sleep labels.
Total diffusion magnitude was lower in N2 for 97/100 people; numerical abscissa and reactivity-gap contrasts also had negative medians.
Effective diffusion dimension and concentration were more heterogeneous.
These are associations in recording-parent estimators, not isolated stage effects or identified mechanisms.

articles.title: Reality from Noise: Same Place, Different Futures — Part 1: How Your Brain Charts What Happens Next
articles.source_path: Reality from Noise essay v2/Reality from Noise - Same Place, Different Futures part 1.typ
articles.abstract: The first essay part shifts from describing a measured neural state to asking what nearby futures remain available and what may change them. It presents MNPS as a map of measured features, rhythms and physiology as candidate controls, and distinguishes chart-level observations from latent neural claims.
takeaways: An MNPS point is a chart location, not a complete description of brain state or experience.
The essay introduces the path from present state to local law, possible futures, and candidate control.
It separates association, mechanism discrimination, ordering recovery, and operator identification.
The cited datasets do not validate the whole biological-control-to-experience chain.

articles.title: Reality from Noise: Same Place, Different Futures — Part 2: Texture, Nudge, and Nearby Horizons
articles.source_path: Reality from Noise essay v2/Reality from Noise - Same Place, Different Futures part 2.typ
articles.abstract: The second part explains how feature texture, local deformation, short-horizon predictive spread, and matched-state control answer different questions. It presents 9D coordinates as a finer measurement chart and emphasizes that a specified estimator does not validate its interpretation.
takeaways: The essay separates C1 sufficiency, C2 added predictive information, and C3 matched-state control claims.
A 9D chart can expose variation hidden by a 3D composite but remains a measurement map.
Local Jacobians, predictive spread, and occupancy are distinct objects.
The proposed tests require held-out comparisons and matched-state controls.

articles.title: Reality from Noise: Same Place, Different Futures — Part 3: When the Horizon Narrows
articles.source_path: Reality from Noise essay v2/Reality from Noise - Same Place, Different Futures part 3.typ
articles.abstract: The third part surveys sleep and clinical applications across depression, psychosis, Parkinson disease, coma, and dementia. It compares which measurement layers carry reported signals and keeps cohort, validity, and inferential limits visible.
takeaways: The essay distinguishes event-level sleep findings from descriptive stage associations.
Clinical examples are organized by the signal-bearing layer rather than one universal disease geometry.
The coma and dementia sections retain support and validation boundaries.
It presents the evidence as bounded rather than end-to-end validation of NDT.

articles.title: Reality from Noise: Same Place, Different Futures — Part 4: The Synthetic Mind
articles.source_path: Reality from Noise essay v2/Reality from Noise - Same Place, Different Futures part 4.typ
articles.abstract: The fourth part connects NDT vocabulary with synthetic-memory and AI projects, discussing SPIRALbase, Hybrid-J, and SPIRAL Cortex. It frames them as engineering demonstrations and speculative bridges, not validation of the biological theory.
takeaways: The essay asks how synthetic systems might retain, retrieve, and adapt information over time.
It describes SPIRALbase, Hybrid-J, and SPIRAL Cortex as candidate memory and policy architectures.
The NDT-SPIRAL bridge shares terms for state, dynamics, control, and memory.
Stronger claims about biological or synthetic minds are marked speculative.

articles.title: Noetic Diffusion Article Summaries: Scientific Review of the Core Theoretical and Empirical Manuscripts
articles.source_path: Reality from Noise essay v2/Reality from Noise - Noetic Diffusion Article Summary part 5 (Article Summary).typ
articles.abstract: This review compiles structured summaries of theoretical and empirical manuscripts on NDT, its measurement frameworks, and related computational, sleep, and clinical work. It is a synthesis for technical review and integration, not a new empirical study.
takeaways: Manuscripts are summarized under abstract, method, results, and discussion sections.
The review spans theory, MNPS/MNJ measurement, and clinical, sleep, altered-state, and computational work.
It tracks the published corpus where a stable source manuscript is available.
The document reports no new data collection or analysis.

articles.title: Autonomic Phase-Locking Is Strongest at Slow-Oscillation Troughs, Not Spindle Onsets, Across Human NREM and REM Sleep
articles.source_path: RichSLeep_EAP_v2/Autonomic Phase-Locking Is Strongest at Slow-Oscillation Troughs, Not Spindle Onsets, Across Human NREM and REM Sleep.typ
articles.abstract: This RichSleep study applies a common phase-locking test across sleep carriers and examines spindle onset under three null constructions. Slow-oscillation locking was strongest, REM-theta coupling was null, onset conclusions depended on null construction, and spindle strength did not robustly moderate the companion geometry association.
takeaways: Slow-oscillation phase locking exceeded other tested carriers.
REM-theta phase locking was null on both channels.
Three onset-null constructions disagreed; the disagreement is reported without choosing a preferred null.
None of 18 prespecified spindle-strength moderation tests survived BH-FDR.

articles.title: Sleep Spindles Briefly Shift Cortical Network Geometry in Two Independent Overnight EEG Datasets
articles.source_path: RVC_SLEEP/Sleep Spindles Briefly Shift Cortical Network Geometry in Two Independent Overnight EEG Datasets.typ
articles.abstract: This study tests spindle-related changes in a nine-coordinate EEG chart across ANPHY, BOAS, and RichSleep recordings. Spindle-versus-own-baseline timing contrasts were supported in ANPHY and BOAS but inconclusive in RichSleep; broader matched-N2 contrasts partly reflected baseline differences.
takeaways: The balance-deviation coordinate rose at spindle events in ANPHY and BOAS after permutation correction.
The RichSleep timing test was underpowered and inconclusive.
Several broader matched-N2 differences reflected pre-spindle baseline versus generic N2.
The timing contrast remains the primary test; the broader comparison is not a substitute.

articles.title: Sleep Spindles Phase-Lock to Respiration at Their Amplitude Peak, Not Onset, in Human NREM Sleep
articles.source_path: RVC_SLEEP_peak_analysis/Sleep Spindles Phase-Lock to Respiration at Their Amplitude Peak, Not Onset, in Human NREM Sleep.typ
articles.abstract: A corrected permutation reanalysis tests phase locking across the RichSleep spindle catalog. Onset remained null, while amplitude peaks showed robust respiratory coupling and weaker cardiac coupling; the secondary geometry link was described as fragile and event-timing related.
takeaways: The analysis covered 23,029 detected spindles from 24 subjects.
Onset phase locking remained null for cardiac and respiratory channels.
Respiratory coupling was robust at spindle peak; cardiac coupling was weaker and less consistent.
The secondary geometry association was framed as awaiting independent replication.
